A single failed OIDC token fetch, such as a cloud metadata endpoint timing out, used to leave the driver's token-fetch mutex holding that failure. Every later operation on the affected `MongoClient` then failed with the original error without attempting a new token fetch, and only restarting the process restored authentication. A failed token fetch now affects only the operation that triggered it.

### Support for MongoDB 4.2 is removed
v7.2.0 introduced the experimental `runtimeAdapters` option and, as part of it, replaced the driver’s static import of Node’s `os` module with a runtime `require('os')`. That works in a CommonJS build, but when the driver is bundled into ESM output (e.g. a Vite/esbuild/rollup server build with `"type": "module"`), there is no `require` in module scope, so constructing a client threw `ReferenceError: require is not defined`. - On PostgreSQL, dropping a table no longer drops columns of other tables that share an enum type (#1630; #1633). Every jobs table has the same `status` enum, so dropping one jobs table used to remove `status` from all the others in the schema.
- `alter()` keeps an attribute's values when it renames a core-type attribute (#1631; #1635). On MySQL the rename is a `CHANGE`. On PostgreSQL, `alter()` refuses the rename before changing anything; renaming there comes in 2.4.

Published to PyPI on 2019-04-13, built from this commit. The repository's `version.py` still read `0.11.1`; the version was set only in the uploaded build.

**Changes since 0.11.1**: https://github.com/datajoint/datajoint-python/compare/v0.11.1...v0.11.2

The archived CHANGELOG listed a later 0.11.2 entry (Jul 25, 2019: "Fix #628 - incompatibility with pyparsing 2.4.1"). That fix was released as [0.11.3](https://github.com/datajoint/datajoint-python/releases/tag/v0.11.3).

## What's Changed

> **Unofficial maintenance release.** DataJoint no longer supports versions before 2.0. This release only fixes installation with setuptools 82 and later; the full test suite was not run.

### Bug Fix
- **Remove the `setuptools` pin and the `otumat` dependency** (#1571, @tabedzki): plugin discovery now uses `importlib.metadata` instead of `pkg_resources`, which setuptools 82 removed, and otumat's two helper functions are copied into `datajoint.plugin`. `setuptools` and `otumat` are no lon

**Two PostgreSQL defects in the hidden columns are fixed.** Every platform-managed column — `_job_start_time`, `_job_duration`, `_job_version`, `_prov`, `_singleton` — is now declared in DataJoint notation and compiled through the type system, so each backend's mapping comes from one place. `_job_start_time` had been declared as a bare `timestamp` and so took microsecond precision on PostgreSQL where MySQL got `datetime(3)`, and `migrate.add_job_metadata_columns` built its `ALTER` with backtick-quoted i

Also: braces in a table or attribute comment no longer crash declaration, `alter()` no longer loses an added attribute's declared type, file-protocol stores are safe on Windows, and non-unique foreign-key columns are indexed on PostgreSQL.
